subject: Discovery recap: untethering from proprietary LLM APIs — PulseLogix
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anita Shah <anita@pulselogix.com>, Kevin Ramos <kevin.r@pulselogix.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery — untethering from proprietary LLM APIs

Hi Anita / Kevin,

Thanks again for the intro call today — appreciate you walking through PulseLogix's current stack and the reasons you're exploring alternatives to your current OpenAI / Anthropic dependency. Quick recap to make sure we captured the right priorities and next steps.

Top pain points you shared:
- Cost volatility: token spend spikes on high-traffic query patterns and inference-heavy features.
- Latency and regional variability: users in EU/APAC see inconsistent response times.
- Vendor lock-in / risk: tight coupling to proprietary APIs (rate limits, sudden policy shifts).
- Security & data residency: need stronger control for PII and auditability.
- Model behavior: hallucination concerns and instruction-following for domain-specific prompts.

Current stack (what you confirmed):
- Production features call OpenAI/Anthropic APIs directly via a server-side proxy.
- Embeddings for search and reranking use OpenAI embeddings; results cached in Redis for 6 hours.
- Some latency-sensitive code paths are batched; others are single-shot streaming.

Success criteria you listed:
1) Maintain or improve 95th-percentile latency for user-facing prompts (~<200ms target).
2) Cost per useful token reduced by at least 35% vs current monthly baseline.
3) Parity for embeddings and instruction-following on core prompt set (we'll validate with evals).
4) Data controls: on-prem/VPC option or strong encryption/KMS + audit logs.

Compatibility needs we should prioritize:
- Streaming + function/tool calling support.
- KV cache / prefix cache compatibility for long chat sessions.
- Embeddings API parity (dimensionality + normalization).
- Stable quantized model options for GPU inference.

Initial model shortlist (for feasibility & perf profiling):
- Llama 2 13B (quantized, instruction-tuned) — good performance/cost tradeoff.
- Mistral-Instruct-ish family (medium) — strong instruction-following for short prompts.
- An instruction-tuned Bloom-style open model as fallback for high-safety routes.

Attachments Im sharing: PulseLogix-MAP-20260714.pdf (first-pass mutual action plan) and pulse-compatibility-matrix-20260714.csv (quick mapping of your reqs to capabilities).

Proposed next steps:
- Ben (cc'd) to run a technical compatibility call next week to go over embeddings dimensionality and KV cache mechanics.
- I'll follow up with an initial cost/latency estimate and a short benchmark plan (sample prompts + dataset).
- You to share any redlines on data residency / procurement calendar (Procurement window: end of Q3?).

If that looks right I'll queue time for a technical deep dive — suggested times: Wed/Thu next week (we have morning PT slots open).

Thanks,

Alex Martinez

Alex — thanks for the clear recap, this matches our notes. A few clarifications and asks from our side: 

- Procurement timeline: target decision window is late September (end of Q3) to align with our budgeting cycle — ideally we want a pilot starting early October.
- Security: we will need evidence of SOC2 Type II and a KMS key management flow for any hosted offering; if on-prem is required well need install docs and an SLA addendum.
- Function calls: very important for a subset of our user flows (actions that invoke backend systems). Wed like a short demo showing function-calling in a low-latency config.

Also attaching a short list of critical prompts (sanitized) that we want benchmarked — Ill drop those into the Google Doc link you shared.

On the shortlist, Kevin wonders about safety/guardrails: what mitigation patterns do you recommend for hallucination-prone sequences?

If Ben can do a 45-min technical session next Wed 9–10am PT that would work.

—Anita
